---
title: "What works with what"
---

Each kernel was fitted to a small simulated data set (24 species, one in the
tree but not fitted) and every feature was tried; ✓ means it ran, – means it
is not defined for that kernel (see the notes). Kernels without a `k_white()`
term behave like the same kernel with one. The table is made by
`data-raw/capabilities.R` in the package sources, so it can be rerun after any
change.

| Kernel | Maximum likelihood | Bayesian (HMC) | loo() | loo_refit() | loo_group() | predict(), fitted species | predict(), new species | ancestral() | se | Several rows per species | ... loo() | ... predict(), new species | ... with se | phylo_gp_trees() + loo() |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k_bm() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_lambda()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_kappa() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_delta() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_eb() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_ou() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_bm() + k_white(df = 4)` | – <sup>a</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_relaxed() + k_white()` | – <sup>a</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_rate_time(5) + k_white()` | – <sup>a</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_bm() + k_dist() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – <sup>b</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_regime() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_edge() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_bm() + k_slope(x) * k_bm() + k_white()` | – <sup>a</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – <sup>c</sup> | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `k_bm() + k_slope(x, latent = FALSE) * k_bm() + k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – <sup>b</sup> | ✓ | – <sup>d</sup> |  |  | – <sup>d</sup> | ✓ |
| `k_bm() + k_slope(x) * k_white()` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – <sup>d</sup> |  |  | – <sup>d</sup> | ✓ |

Columns starting with ... refer to several rows per species.

<sup>a</sup> Latent values (rates, slopes, t multipliers) are sampled, so these kernels need `method = "sample"`.  
<sup>b</sup> Ancestral states need a process along the tree; dense components (`k_dist()`, `k_slope(latent = FALSE)`) have none.  
<sup>c</sup> Ancestral states are not defined for varying slopes (the slope at a node has no trait value).  
<sup>d</sup> With several rows per species, use one latent `k_slope(x) * k` term with a branch-wise `k`.
